summary.headline: Chola disbursements rose 47% YoY to INR35,872 crore and AUM 25% to INR2,68,009 crore; Board approved up to INR5,000 crore capital raise.
summary.overview: Q2 FY27 showed broad-based growth across vehicle finance, SME and consumer loans, with AUM up 25% YoY and disbursements up 47%. Credit costs fell 37 bps YoY and PBT ROA expanded 40 bps, with ROE at 19.4% versus 18.1% a year ago. Gross Stage 3 eased to 3.25% from 3.29% QoQ. The Board approved a proposal to raise up to INR5,000 crore, though management said timing depends on market conditions, with a possible window of six to nine months. Management did not revise FY27 guidance and flagged drought, rate-hike and insurance-commission risks as under watch.

segments.name: Vehicle finance
segments.commentary: Disbursements INR17,801 crore (+31% YoY), AUM INR1,29,787 crore (+21%). Management says Chola grew materially ahead of industry; October disbursements trending +18-20% YoY, and Q3 guided at +20-22%.

segments.name: SME finance (LAP, SME, SBPL)
segments.commentary: Disbursements INR9,345 crore (+42%). AUM INR72,356 crore (+27%): LAP INR57,447 crore (+24%), SME INR10,943 crore (+45%), SBPL INR3,966 crore (+35%).

segments.name: Consumer loans (home, CSEL, gold)
segments.commentary: Disbursements INR8,726 crore (+103%), AUM INR45,902 crore (+32%): home loans INR25,240 crore, CSEL INR17,216 crore, gold INR3,446 crore. Disbursement growth in home loans 43%, CSEL 103%, gold 320%.

segments.name: CSEL pre-tax ROA
segments.commentary: Consumer durables plus digital lending and unsecured business/personal loans currently earn ~3.6% pre-tax ROA; management sees >4% medium term, with segment disclosure deferred.

guidance_outlook: FY27 growth guidance not revised; management said outcomes could be better given stronger Q3/Q4 seasonality, but it does not believe raising guidance is prudent now.
Net credit cost guided at ~1.4% for the full year; already achieved in H1 per management.
Cost of funds expected to rise ~15-20 bps YoY for the full year (assuming 50 bps of repo hikes, 25 bps already and 25 bps more); second half to be higher, first half lower.
Yields expected to see a modest decline of ~10 bps; management expects credit-cost improvement to more than offset this, with ROTA better than last year.
Opex ratio expected to stay at 3.0-3.1% near term, with a long-term aim of ~2.8% over 2-3 years.
Steady-state AUM growth guided at 20-23%; PBT ROA guidance anchored at 3.5%, with no change to be considered until new businesses scale.
Repricing of floating-rate home loan and LAP books planned for Q3; affordable housing, LAP and floating book being evaluated for pricing action over 1-2 months.
Capital raise of up to INR5,000 crore, possibly in 6-9 months, form (equity or equity plus convertible instruments) to be decided later; enabling shareholder resolution obtained.
capex_capacity: Plan to open ~360 branches in FY27 after 120 last year; management stressed branch openings depend on productivity, with Phase 1 branches averaging ~INR21 crore AUM and a 15-20 crore threshold for Phase 2.
Combined 1,595 branches plus 689 resident location hubs (RLHs); ~125 RLHs being converted to full branches.
Assigned book target kept at 5-7% of total book; no assignment deal done beyond one this quarter.
Capital raise up to INR5,000 crore approved by Board; CCDs fully converted to equity as of September 2026.
demand_pricing: Industry: HCV grew ~40% in Q2 and ~20% in H1 (highest-ever H1); LCV +25%, SCV ~+26%, PV +31%, two-wheelers +15% in Q2. Management expects 15-20% industry growth in H2 under a conservative case.
Festive season spread across October and November this year versus concentration in October last year; base effect supports Q3.
Management says roughly 40% of business originates in the South; 60% from North, East and West.
Customer mix: vehicle ~52%, home loans ~10%, LAP ~22%; mortgages ~36-37% combined, to rise over 3-4 years. Consumer, gold and CSEL to stay within 15% in near term.

Consumer durables disbursement growth partly reflects a low base; management says Q2 volumes are back to earlier levels of INR1,000-1,200 crore per month. CD is majority of CSEL disbursement growth, unsecured business and personal loans ~40%.
Gold loans are almost entirely bullet structure (12-month tenor); EMI-based loans ~1% of book.
Small-ticket LAP averages INR15-20 lakh ticket size; monthly disbursement run-rate ~INR500 crore per quarter cited for SLAP.

Drought impact: rainfall deficit ~13%, concentrated in Vidarbha, Malwa, parts of MP and coastal Karnataka; tractors ~3% of vehicle finance book. Management sees no meaningful stress yet, with clarity expected by December.

qa_highlights.question: Is the INR5,000 crore capital raise imminent and what is the three-year growth and segment strategy?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the raise is to strengthen the balance sheet and is not imminent; it will be done in the near to medium term depending on markets, possibly within 6-9 months. Growth will come mainly from scaling existing businesses.

qa_highlights.question: What is the cost of funds sensitivity to rate hikes?
qa_highlights.answer: Cost of funds may rise ~15-20 bps for FY27 (about 15 bps per later clarification), including an assumed 50 bps of hikes; ~25% of borrowings are repo-linked and ~25% linked to other benchmarks, with the rest fixed or MCLR-based.

qa_highlights.question: Will opex stay in the 3.0-3.1% range?
qa_highlights.answer: Employee cost rose as outsourced staff moved onto payroll (~INR100 crore shifted from outsourcing QoQ); Q2 also included July salary revisions and a one-time business meet cost. Opex ratio to stay ~3.0-3.1%, with occasional quarterly variation.

qa_highlights.question: Why did aggregate yield fall ~30 bps while segment yields rose?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed the drop mainly to the absence of gain-on-assignment income (only one deal this quarter, about 20 bps impact). Assignment limits with banks are exhausted for now.

qa_highlights.question: Is there a risk of tighter asset quality from drought in vehicle finance?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said drought-prone regions were deliberately underweighted, tractor exposure has been reduced, and no material stress is visible; H2 asset quality expected to be better than H1.

qa_highlights.question: Are home loan and LAP disbursement numbers sustainable after the Q1 reporting alignment?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said a technical alignment of disbursement reporting shifted some Q1 volumes; underlying Q2 was marginally better than Q1 and growth was helped by a low base.

qa_highlights.question: What is the insurance distribution reform impact?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it has modelled scenarios and will offset any loss of insurance income through other levers, but is awaiting clarity on the final outcome before quantifying impact.

risks_watch: Drought and weak rainfall in Vidarbha, Malwa, MP and coastal Karnataka; December assessment on Rabi sowing and reservoir levels.
Cost of funds pressure from rate hikes; MCLR-linked funding expected to move up gradually, with bigger impact likely in FY28.
Insurance distribution (credit-life commission) reform could reduce insurance income; quantification pending.
Yield pressure from absence of assignment income and possible ~10 bps decline in yield for the year.
Base effects in H2 may moderate YoY growth, and management has not revised guidance.
Gold loan bullet-structure book at ~12-month tenor; branch scale-up pace depends on Phase 2 productivity reaching INR15-20 crore.
Capital raise size, structure and timing still undecided; dilution impact unknown.
summary.management_tone: Confident on growth, asset quality and October trends, but cautious and noncommittal on drought, insurance-income impact and guidance changes. Management repeatedly deferred specifics (segment disclosures, one-time costs, capital raise form and timing) and said it will wait for clarity before quantifying.
key_quotes: Given this backdrop, a key focus area is ensuring that our capital position remains strong enough to support this growth trajectory.
We still hold to that 20% to 23% on a steady -state basis, because there are volatilities that is possible.
At this stage, the proposal should be viewed primarily as a measure to maintain strategic flexibility rather than an indication of an imminent capital raise
Historically, drought-prone regions such as Vidarbha, Malwa, Coastal Karnataka, and parts of Madhya Pradesh have been relatively challenging for us from a portfolio performance perspective.

adds.what: ~360 new branches planned in FY27 (after 120 last year), Phase 1 branches averaging ~INR21 crore AUM
~125 resident location hubs being converted to full branches

growth.why: FY27 AUM/disbursement growth guidance held at 20-23% steady state (about 25% achieved in H1), with no upgrade; delivery backed by ~360 planned branch openings, Q3 vehicle guidance of +20-22%, and industry H2 growth of 15-20%, though no order-book or quantified capacity figures tie the guidance together.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: Cost of funds guided +15-20 bps YoY for FY27 and yields seen down ~10 bps, but credit cost held at ~1.4% (already achieved in H1) and PBT ROA anchored at 3.5%, so margin support depends on credit-cost relief offsetting funding and yield pressure.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: Plan to open ~360 branches in FY27 after 120 last year, on top of 1,595 branches and ~125 RLH-to-branch conversions; branch openings depend on Phase 2 productivity of INR15-20 crore AUM.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: AUM +25% and disbursements +47% YoY in H1 against a 20-23% steady-state guide; Q3 vehicle guided +20-22%, industry H2 growth seen at 15-20%, though base effects may moderate YoY growth.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Capex and utilisation were not discussed; the business is branch-led and asset-light, and the Rs 5,000 crore capital raise is for balance-sheet strength rather than a new capex programme.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Management explicitly held FY27 guidance and said raising it is not prudent now, although outcomes could be better given stronger Q3/Q4 seasonality.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Drought (~13% rainfall deficit, tractors ~3% of vehicle book), rate hikes (50 bps assumed, MCLR funding bigger in FY28) and insurance commission reform are under watch, with clarity due by December.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: No new product or model launch was discussed; growth is from scaling existing vehicle, SME, LAP, home and CSEL businesses.

rows.label: Repricing of floating home loan and LAP books
rows.why: Repricing of floating-rate home loan and LAP books is planned for Q3, with affordable housing, LAP and floating book pricing under evaluation over 1-2 months, which could offset the ~10 bps yield decline.

rows.label: INR5,000 crore capital raise
rows.why: Board approved up to INR5,000 crore with enabling shareholder resolution, but timing depends on markets and form (equity or equity plus convertibles) is undecided, so dilution is unknown.

rows.label: Insurance distribution (credit-life commission) reform
rows.why: Reform could reduce insurance income; management has modelled scenarios and will offset via other levers but has not quantified impact pending clarity.

tone.note: Management was confident on growth, October trends and asset quality (Stage 3 down to 3.25%), but cautious and noncommittal on drought, insurance-income impact, capital raise timing and guidance changes; analysts pressed on yield decline, cost of funds and opex.
